This missense change has been observed in individual(s) with cystic fibrosis (PMID: 1710599, 15638824, 23974870, 29133775). In at least one individual the data is consistent with being in trans (on the opposite chromosome) from a pathogenic variant. ClinVar contains an entry for this variant (Variation ID: 48692). Invitae Evidence Modeling of protein sequence and biophysical properties (such as structural, functional, and spatial information, amino acid conservation, physicochemical variation, residue mobility, and thermodynamic stability) indicates that this missense variant is expected to disrupt CFTR protein function with a positive predictive value of 80%. Experimental studies have shown that this missense change affects CFTR function (PMID: 9305991). For these reasons, this variant has been classified as Pathogenic.</Comment>

Five of five in-silico tools predict a damaging effect of the variant on protein function. One computational tool predict the variant creates a 3' acceptor site. Consistent with this prediction, one functional study showed that this variant led to a significant skipping of exon 5 (Raynal_2013). The variant allele was found at a frequency of 1.2e-05 in 168188 control chromosomes. c.532G>A has been reported in the literature in multiple individuals affected with Cystic Fibrosis (Zielenski_1991, Cremonesi_1992, Heim_2001, Sugarman_2004, Ooi_2012, Sosnay_2013, DeBoeck_2014).
